rules.meaning: a slide is drawn smaller or larger than the canvas, so its page shows an empty band or loses an edge
rules.suggestion: make each <section> exactly the canvas size and let its content fill it

rules.meaning: a box carries a thick colored stripe along one side only, the side-tab or top-bar accent
rules.suggestion: remove the stripe; mark the box with a tinted fill, an even hairline border on every side, type weight or an icon

rules.meaning: text is set below presentation size at the 1600px canvas: body text under 28px or a caption or label under 20px
rules.suggestion: raise body text to 28px and captions to 20px or more, and cut words until it fits; a slide holds less text rather than smaller text

rules.meaning: a short word, number or price is split across two lines inside itself
rules.suggestion: widen the column or the cell until the word fits on one line, or set the text smaller within the type scale; a word is never broken

rules.meaning: a chart is drawn so small that its marks vanish and only its labels show
rules.suggestion: give the chart a width and a height of its own, at least 320 by 240 px, instead of letting it shrink inside a flex box

rules.meaning: the text and pictures of a content or data page stop high while its cards, columns or panels run on down, so its lower part shows empty boxes
rules.suggestion: fill the lower part with what the page already holds: set the numbers, headings, body text, chart or photo larger so the content reaches about 100px from the bottom edge, and make each card or panel as tall as what it holds; never spread a card's parts apart, stretch a box or add words to fill the space

rules.meaning: a content or data page leaves a band across its whole width empty, most often its lower part, because its parts end high or sit centered in a taller area; a hairline or a column's side border draws nothing that fills it
rules.suggestion: give the page fewer, larger parts: set the main number, chart, table or photo large enough to take the space between the title and about 100px above the bottom edge, set the type larger, and start it near the title instead of centering a short block; when a box of set height holds everything, size that box rather than what is inside it; when the page has too little to say for a full slide and the slide count allows, merge it into the page before or after it; never stretch a box or a divider over the band, and never add words to fill it

rules.meaning: a card or panel on a content or data page leaves a large stretch of its height empty, above, between or below what it holds, most often a box stretched to fill the page around one number or a line or two pushed to its ends
rules.suggestion: make the box fit what it holds instead of stretching it: drop the box and set the number or line large on the page, give the card the explanation and figures it is about, or join thin cards into one list or table; when the page then has too little to say and the slide count allows, merge it into the page before or after it; never add words or a decorative bar to fill the box

rules.meaning: a part of the slide is drawn partly or wholly outside the slide, so it is cut off at the edge
rules.suggestion: keep every part inside the slide: move or resize it, shorten the text that runs past, or split the slide

rules.meaning: content is drawn outside the box that should hold it, a card, a filled or bordered area or a clipping frame, so it spills out or is cut off
rules.suggestion: give the box room for its content or take the overflowing part out: shorten the text, drop a fixed height, or move the part into a box of its own

rules.meaning: two parts of the slide are drawn over each other: text over text, text over a logo, icon, picture or box
rules.suggestion: move one of them apart from the other, or shorten the text, so no two parts overlap; a part that fills most of the slide is a background and is the one overlap allowed

deckRules.meaning: a content or data page sets its content as the same arrangement of equal cards (the same row, column or grid of as many cards) as the page before it or as two earlier pages, so the deck reads as one slide repeated
deckRules.suggestion: compose this page another way that fits its layout: columns divided by thin rules instead of boxes, a numbered list, a table, one lead block beside smaller ones, a large figure with its context, or cards of different sizes; keep the words and figures
